statement: Every T1 topological space (one in which all singletons are closed) is Hausdorff.
definitions: Hausdorff (T2) = any two distinct points have disjoint open neighbourhoods. T1 as defined in the statement (all singletons closed).
ground_truth_witness: The integers Z with the finite complement (cofinite) topology: the open sets are the empty set and the sets whose complement is finite. Each singleton {n} is closed because Z minus {n} has finite complement. But no two points can be separated by disjoint open sets: two nonempty open sets U = Z minus F1 and V = Z minus F2 (F1, F2 finite) always share every integer larger than every element of F1 union F2, so U intersect V is nonempty.
reference_authority: published counterexample (book-cited), verified per partB_feasibility records
verification_note: Checked exactly on an explicit 31-member family of cofinite sets given by their finite complements inside [-20,20]: closure of the family shape under pairwise union and intersection (complement algebra verified pointwise on the window [-25,25] and by finiteness of the complement lists), closedness of sampled singletons, and for every pair of nonempty members an explicit common integer max(F1 union F2)+1. Cited: the infinitude of Z, which makes every cofinite set nonempty, so the sampled intersection argument applies to arbitrary pairs.
book_citation: Lynn Arthur Steen and J. Arthur Seebach Jr., Counterexamples in Topology, 2nd ed., Springer-Verlag, 1978 (Dover reprint, 1995), Example 18 (Finite complement topology on a countable space)

skeptic.objection: Precise (T1 is defined in the statement) and false. Reference argument is correct: in the cofinite topology on Z every singleton is closed, and any two nonempty open sets have finite complements, hence intersect. Short but genuine two-part verification (T1 holds, T2 fails). Not a duplicate: surplus cb-topo-001 is the T0-vs-T1 claim with the Sierpinski space.
skeptic.suggested_definitions: Hausdorff (T2) = any two distinct points have disjoint open neighbourhoods. T1 as defined in the statement (all singletons closed).
